blocks.text: Setting up your project coordinator workspace

Your workspace needs a clear hierarchy to remain useful. Start by creating a main project dashboard. Use linked databases to pull in tasks from various projects into one view. This prevents the need to jump between pages constantly.

items: Create a master tasks database with properties for status, priority, and assignee.
Use templates for recurring meeting notes to ensure consistency.
Implement a project status property using a select or status type.
Group tasks by project using the board view for visual clarity.

blocks.text: Essential Notion shortcuts for Mac users

Efficiency on a Mac comes from keeping your hands on the keyboard. Use the `/` key to open the block menu. Press ⌘ + P to open the search bar and jump between pages in seconds. Press ⇧ + ? to view the full list of shortcuts.
If you find yourself creating the same page structure repeatedly, stop. Create a database template instead. This saves you from manual setup every time you start a new project phase.
blocks.title: Use templates

blocks.text: Lazur lives in your Mac menu bar. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are lost in a complex Notion database, ask Lazur where a specific property or filter is. It will draw a circle around the element.

Documentation is the lifeblood of coordination. Use toggles to hide detailed notes while keeping the main page clean. Link related documents using the @ mention feature to create a web of information that is easy to follow.

Keep your stakeholders informed by creating a dedicated status report page. Use a linked database view filtered to show only high priority items or items due this week. This provides an instant snapshot of project health.
